problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration, measured in $\text{m}/{\text{s}}^{2},$ given by the function $a(t)=2t+{t}^{2}$, where $t$ is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity $v=\frac{8}{3}\,\text{m}/\text{s}$ when $t=1\,\text{s}$, calculate the velocity of the particle at the moment $t=2\,\text{s}.$
worked_solution:
First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\text{d}t \\  & =\int (2t+{t}^{2})\text{d}t \\  & ={t}^{2}+\frac{{t}^{3}}{3}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(1)=\frac{8}{3}.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{8}{3} & =(1)^{2}+\frac{(1)^{3}}{3}+C \\ \frac{8}{3} & =1+\frac{1}{3}+C \\ C & =\frac{4}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)=\frac{4}{3}+{t}^{2}+\frac{{t}^{3}}{3}.$

We evaluate the velocity at time $t=2\,\text{s}$:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(2) & =\frac{4}{3}+(2)^{2}+\frac{(2)^{3}}{3} \\  & =\frac{4}{3}+4+\frac{8}{3} \\  & =8\,\text{m/s}\end{aligned}
$$
